messages:
maya: quick heads-up — running the quant shootout for Mistral-3 (1B & 8B) and seeing reproducible structured-output regressions only on the AWQ -> TensorRT-LLM path with CUDA 13.1. GPTQ baseline and vLLM path look fine. logs attached.

sam: can you paste a tiny failing eval and the exact quant config? bits, per-channel/per-tensor, bias correction?

maya: config: AWQ 4-bit, per-channel scales, quantize_bias=true, awq-convert v0.9.2, trt-llm driver v0.6. Tested with GPTQ 4-bit (our gptq-convert v0.8) — GPTQ result matches float baseline. Only trt path regresses on structured output fields.

maya: failing example (expected vs actual from our structured eval):
```
expected: {"name":"The Bakery","rating":4.7,"hours":{"open":7,"close":17}}
actual (trt-awq): {"name":"The Bakery","rating":4.2}  // missing hours block, numeric drift on rating
```

kai: odd — sounds like token truncation or attention mask misalignment rather than numeric quant noise. Does the output truncate mid-object or drop nested fields?

maya: consistently drops nested fields after the first object key in many cases. not random cutoff; pattern looks deterministic per prompt.

oscar: have you checked KV-cache offsets? TRT-LLM had one change where it optimized kv packing for FP8 paths; could be index math bug on CUDA13.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: pushed image trtllm:cuda13-2024-10 to staging at 2024-10-12T09:32:00Z.

sam: can you reproduce with batch_size=1 and disable batching? also try TRT_LOGGER_LEVEL=VERBOSE to look for plugin fallback messages.

maya: repro steps (short):
1) quantize model with awq-convert --bits 4 --per-channel
2) start trt-llm server with trtllm:cuda13-2024-10 image, batch_size=1
3) run structured eval set `structured_eval_v2.json`

Logs snippet from trt-llm server (verbose):
```
[TRT] Plugin "awq_int8_dequant" falling back to fp16 kernel for layer_21
[TRT] Warning: Plugin runtime dtype mismatch for attention_kv_pack, performing slow path
[TRT] KV pack offset computed: 0x7ff... expected 0x7fe... // suspicious off-by-one
```

kai: that "falling back to fp16 kernel" is suspicious. if TRT changes internal packing when kernel fallback happens, attention indices could misalign for structured outputs. GPTQ may not trigger that plugin.

oscar: also check NCCL/p2p logs if you're running multi-gpu; we saw peer-to-peer memcpy reorder on CUDA 13 with certain driver combos. any multi-gpu here?

maya: tests were single-GPU (A100 80GB) — no NCCL. but we did hit occasional OOM-like fragmentation when running 8B model with batch>1. single-gpu, batch=1 still exhibits the structured-field drop though.

eval-bot: regression summary for AWQ->TRT (vs float baseline): EM down 7.4%, avg F1 -5.2 pts, structured field recall -12% (n=360 prompts). GPTQ->TRT shows EM -0.8% only. vLLM-AWQ path EM -0.9%.

sam: two hypotheses: 1) TRT AWQ plugin has a dtype fallback that changes KV packing/layout; 2) CUDA13 driver + trtllm combined triggered a codepath we didn't hit on CUDA12. Try container with CUDA12 + trtllm same commit.

maya: tried CUDA12 image (trtllm:cuda12-2024-08) — AWQ->TRT on cuda12 passes baseline. so looks like CUDA13 interaction.

kai: can you bisect the trt-llm container commits too? maybe a recent plugin optimization introduced the issue but only manifests with CUDA13.

oscar: quick repro patch to try: force the plugin to use consistent dtype path by setting env `TRT_PLUGIN_FORCE_FP16=0` (temporary internal test var) and restart server. also run with `TRT_LOGGER_LEVEL=VERBOSE` + `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` to surface any silent misorders.

maya: tried forcing fp16 off — still reproduces. forcing AWQ plugin to use pure fp32 path (big perf hit) fixes the regression, so layout/packing seems to be the culprit.

sam: can you capture the first 8k bytes of the packed KV buffer before it goes into the plugin for both CUDA12 and CUDA13 runs and diff them? if offsets differ we'll see the off-by-one.

maya: doing that now — uploading diffs to the thread shortly.

eval-bot: note: structured suite contains many small JSON-like outputs which are sensitive to tokenization boundary changes; even a single token misalign can drop a whole nested field. suggests attention/KV mis-indexing rather than numeric rounding.

oscar: another check — is the tokenizer version identical across runs? different tokenizers can change token boundaries making structured outputs fragile.

maya: tokenizer v2.1.0 in both. confirmed.

kai: provisional plan:
- maya: capture KV buffer dumps (cuda12 vs cuda13) + minimal repro payloads (today)
- sam: spin up a cuda13 image with trt-llm pinned to previous plugin commit (tomorrow)
- oscar: open an upstream TRT-LLM issue with kernel fallback logs + repro artifacts (tomorrow)
- kai: run quick patch replacing awq plugin packing logic with the cuda12-compatible codepath to see if that removes regression (end of week)

maya: uploaded diffs: looks like a 16-byte offset shift in the packed KV buffer for the CUDA13 run. attaching hex excerpt.

sam: that lines up with a pack-alignment change in the CUDA13 runtime for certain intrinsics. I’ll repro locally and try forcing 16-byte alignment shim to validate.

oscar: opened issue https://github.com/trt-llm/trt-llm/issues/482 with logs + minimal repro tarball. link shared.

maya: thanks — will wait for upstream feedback. for now we'll avoid promoting AWQ->TRT on cuda13 to staging. switching to vLLM for nightly AWQ metrics until fixed. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

sam: +1. create a short release note/flag in the rollout doc so SRE knows to avoid cuda13 trt-awq for customer-facing Dedicated pools.

kai: adding to rollout checklist and tagging ops.

maya: thx everyone. will post updates when upstream responds or when we have a patch. :rocket:
